title: Introduce windowed-egress-sink and soft-circuit rate limiter
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a windowed regional egress sink to provide a short-duration safety net for bursty cross-region egress surges and a soft circuit rate limiter that throttles non-critical traffic early to protect SLO-critical paths.
description:
Motivation: We observed several incidents where sudden cross-region egress spikes (large batch inference jobs or misconfigured clients) saturated downstream egress quotas and caused noisy evictions that then cascaded into SLO violations for latency-sensitive routes. This PR implements a conservative, temporary 'egress sink' window and a soft circuit-style rate limiter to give the control plane a deterministic short-duration buffer to rehydrate KV caches, avoid mass evictions, and maintain tail latency for critical routes.

What this changes (summary): - Windowed egress sink: per-region ephemeral sink queue that accepts a bounded amount of outgoing traffic for a configurable window (default 45s). The sink is non-dropping for high-priority requests and acts as a spill buffer for lower-priority traffic. If the sink fills, older low-priority items are gently delayed/retried with backoff. - Soft circuit rate limiter: a lightweight token-based soft circuit that reduces admitted qps for non-SLO critical tiers (e.g., background embeddings, bulk-embedding jobs) when egress utilization exceeds a soft threshold. The limiter emits rich telemetry and a short-lived circuit-open signal that does not orphan requests; it prefers throttling+retry hints to hard rejects. - Topology-aware routing adjustments: during sink windows we steer best-effort traffic to regions with spare egress headroom before opening the sink to minimize cross-region cost. - Config + runtime flags: new runtime knobs (region.sink.enabled, region.sink.size_mb, region.sink.window_s, region.soft_cb.threshold_pct, region.soft_cb.cooldown_s) with safe defaults.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (internal) linked: LIN-7842 - [x] Unit tests for sink queue and limiter logic - [x] Integration test with regional egress simulator - [x] Metrics + tracing added (egress.sink_fill_ratio, softcb.open_events, softcb.throttle_rate) - [x] Feature-flag rollout via runtime flags - [x] Docs snippet for on-call playbook

Commits (high-level): - 9a1b2c add sink queue data structure and persistence hook - 2b3c4d integrate sink admission controller into egress pipeline - 4d5e6f soft-circuit limiter implementation and tests - 7e8f90 add topology-aware steering and config - a1b2c3 telemetry, tracing, and docs snippet - d4e5f6 revert tweaks after reviewer feedback

Files changed (high-level): - src/egress/sink_queue.go: new sink queue implementation and bounded eviction policy - src/egress/admit_controller.go: admission flow with sink checks and priority decisions - src/egress/soft_cb.go: soft circuit limiter, token accounting, cooldown logic - src/config/runtime_defaults.yaml: new runtime knobs and docs - tests/egress/sink_simulator_test.go: integration test that simulates cross-region egress pressure - docs/oncall/egress-sink-playbook.md: short runbook for on-call when sink triggers - pkg/telemetry/metrics_registry.go: new metrics registration

Design notes and algorithm: - Sink sizing: default size is 200MB per-region, window 45s. Sizing picked to cover typical 95th-percentile burst sizes observed in telemetry while keeping memory footprint bounded. - Admission logic: requests are assigned a priority tag (critical, interactive, best-effort). Critical always bypasses sink and soft-cb. Interactive will go to sink if sink has capacity; best-effort is steered or admitted to sink. - Soft-cb algorithm: moving-window utilization estimate U(t). If U(t) > threshold (default 78%), we open soft-cb for low-priority tiers and compute throttle fraction f = clamp((U - threshold) / (100 - threshold), 0, 0.9). We then sample admission for best-effort requests with probability 1 - f and emit telemetry. Cooldown uses exponential backoff with jitter to avoid synchronized reopen storms. - Observability: every sink admission emits a trace event with sink_fill_ratio and route_hint. softcb emits open/close events and per-tier throttle_rate gauge.

Review conversation (highlights): - Liam: "Can we ensure that sink state does not persist across node restarts and therefore cause stale admission?" -> Maya: "Sink queue is in-memory per node with optional transient persistence only for graceful restarts; default disabled. Added docs and tests to ensure restart clears queues unless feature is explicitly configured." - Rina: "Telemetry cardinality concern — don't emit per-request tags in metrics." -> Maya: "Adjusted traces to sample 1% and added aggregated metrics only (fill_ratio by region)." - Diego: "What happens if the sink fills and clients retry aggressively?" -> Maya: "Added backoff-on-retry guidance in docs and the admission controller now annotates responses with Retry-After headers for best-effort lanes." - Liam (post-approval): "Small nit: rename SoftCB::threshold to soft_threshold_pct for clarity." -> fixed in commit d4e5f6.

CI and verification: - Unit: passed (all tests green) - Integration: egress-simulation matrix passed in 3/4 topologies; one flaky topology retried and green on re-run - Lint: warnings fixed - Load test: local perf run shows sub-1% SLO regression on interactive latency under burst; best-effort qps reduced as expected.

Fallback and rollout plan: - Feature gated behind runtime flag region.sink.enabled=false by default - Canary rollout to region-us-west-2 (20% of nodes) for 48h, monitor egress.sink_fill_ratio, interactive p99 latency, softcb.open_events - If softcb.open_events > 0.5/min for more than 30m or interactive p99 regresses > 5%, auto-disable via ops playbook.

Post-merge actions: - Follow-up PR to add per-tenant policies in sink admission (next; ENG-7843) - Ops runbook added to docs but will be extended with run frequency graphs and alert thresholds (ENG-7844)

Why this is different: Unlike previous hard-circuit or blunt eviction strategies, the windowed egress sink acts as a short-duration pressure-relief buffer that preserves critical request paths and gives the control plane a deterministic time window to react. The soft circuit introduces probabilistic throttling for non-critical tiers (favoring graceful retry and observability over silent drops). This pattern reduces oscillation and mass-eviction cascades observed in recent incidents.
